Policies, Requirements & Guidelines
Our graduate students receive world-class training throughout the Ph.D. program, both as part of their own research projects as well as through core courses and milestone assessments. The expectations for both graduate students and faculty are laid out in the guidelines below.
The Program Policies and Regulations (a.k.a. the Graduate Program Handbook) provides comprehensive information on the requirements and guidelines of the graduate program. Download a PDF copy using the link below.
Download the Graduate Program Handbook
Please contact the Graduate Program Director, Prof. Mike Barnes, for clarification on any aspects of the graduate program policies, requirements, and guidelines.
Students are expected to understand the boundaries of acceptable AI use. Information related to the university's policies can be found at Responsible Use of Generative AI and the department's Graduate Program AI Policy is listed below.
University of Massachusetts Chemistry Graduate Program Policy Statement on Responsible Use of AI
AI is emerging as a power tool in scientific research. However, as soon as you use AI for a task, you are bypassing the opportunity to inject your own creativity and insight into your document. We recommend that you tackle the task yourself first, and then use AI for refinement or other assistance. Once you see the AI output, your ability to add your own creative input will be diminished – it is like seeing the movie before you read the book: you no longer supply your own image of the characters and the settings. Therefore, be mindful of the impact of using AI on your graduate training and expertise.
1. Before you use AI tools, read and follow the guidance provided in the article “Best Practices for Using AI When Writing Scientific Manuscripts” in ACS Nano https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acsnano.3c01544
2. Do NOT upload unpublished research materials, intellectual-property protected content, or FERPA protected data to platforms such as ChatGPT (or similar services), where the data does not remain within UMass-protected systems. The GenAI and Copilot platforms at UMass Amherst are secure platforms and the uploaded data stays within the UMass system.
3. Do NOT use text verbatim from AI bots. These are not your words, and bot output may contain reused text from other sources – direct use could constitute plagiarism. If you use AI to help you brainstorm for a good title, be sure to check that your final title is not the same or too similar to an existing publication.
4. Acknowledgement: In Acknowledgments and Methods sections, you MUST acknowledge your use of an AI such as ChatGPT, Copilot or any other tool to prepare your manuscript or document. In addition, you MUST acknowledge if AI tools were used to help generate research questions. Provide the prompts and questions you used (and/or transcript) as Supporting Information. This is standard publishing policy and best practices for all documents
5. In preparation of exam documents, students shall consult with PI regarding AI use. All exam documents (Prospectus/Original Research Proposal/Dissertation or Thesis) shall include a statement regarding AI use: If no AI output is used, a simple statement to that effect suffices. If AI output is used, a statement of acknowledgment of use, checking and verification, and appropriate editing conforming to published work guidelines is required.
6. AI-based bots (ChatGPT or Copilot) cannot be held accountable for any statement or ethical breach. All authors of the manuscript share the responsibility of the accuracy of the statements made.
7. Checking and rechecking: Remind yourself and coauthors that AI output is incomplete and may contain incorrect information. Check every sentence/statement critically. If using AI language tools for citation
recommendations, be especially sure to verify these citations. You must read each cited article to be sure it contains the material being cited.
8. You are required to follow UMass guidelines on responsible use of AI. See https://www.umass.edu/provost/responsible-use-generative-ai and https://www.umass.edu/studentsuccess/guidance-generative-artificial-intelligence
9. UMass guidelines state that: “Students cannot use Generative AI (ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, etc.) to complete any academic work without instructor permission. If an instructor has not given explicit permission to use Generative AI, students should assume they are not allowed to do so in that course. Students should always receive instructor permission to use Generative AI in any part of completing academic work.”
